newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways strike halts cargo movement.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways strike halts cargo movement.

text.p: Nearly 1,000 cargo handling workers of Thai Airways International Plc went on strike for a second day on Tuesday, paralysing outbound cargo movement of most regional airlines at Bangkok's Don Muang Airport.

Airline industry sources told Reuters several dozen airlines, mostly Asian carriers, were affected by the industrial action, launched by Thai Airways employees to pressure the government to overturn its recent decision to launch a new Thai air cargo carrier.
More than 500 Thai Airways workers also staged a rally at Prime Minister Banharn Silpa's office at Government House in Bangkok on Tuesday.

They demanded that the cabinet change its October 15 decision to launch Thai Air Cargo Co Ltd in which Thai Airways would hold a 40 percent stake. The workers fear that they may be displaced by the launch of the new company.
Clients of Thai Airways in Phnom Penh said they were turned away by airline staff when they tried to ship cargo out of Cambodia.

Thai Airways employees normally handle up to 70 percent of cargoes at the Bangkok airport. Among major airlines hit by the strike were Cathay Pacific Airways, Singapore Airlines, China Airlines, Korean Airlines and Malaysian Airlines.

"The economic damage is quite substantial. Up to seven of our daily flights are affected. A lot of our out-bound cargoes are stranded in the locked warehouse," said an official of Cathay Pacific Airlines.
She said Cathay normally ships about 30-40 tonnes of cargo daily, mostly electronics, garment and textiles, out of Bangkok.
"We are now at the height of the season for the shipping of textiles and garment to Europe for Christmas," she added.
Leaders of the striking workers sought a government guarantee that the new cargo carrier would not affect their jobs or compromise their work benefits and welfare.
They said the decision to form a new carrier was not transparent and alleged that some politicians in the government had pushed for the creation of the carrier to favour some private firms.
Airlines sources said many regional airlines had asked Thai exporters since late last week to cancel shipments of perishable goods like natural flowers, fruits, vegetables and ornamental fishes.

They said more than a dozen airlines, mostly European and American, were unaffected by the work slowdown as their cargoes are handled by separate workers hired by the Airport Authority of Thailand (AAT) which runs the airport.
Among carriers unaffected were Lufthansa Airlines, United Airlines, Air France, Northwest Airlines, and Japan Airlines.
Employees of carriers hit by the strike said Thai Airways workers refused to unlock a warehouse to let stranded cargo be handled by AAT staff.
